decisions.reason: The adjustable quarter-pallet display draws directly on the firm's cardboard display know-how, so in-house R&D can keep adapting it, although its absence from the website since 2020 raises doubt that it is still actively offered.

The pegboard-back shelf display is a small variation on the core competence, so the firm can absorb customer feedback and refine it, but its disappearance from the website signals a real risk of withdrawal.
The standard quarter-pallet shelf display is a core format built on existing knowledge and capacity, so it is the most likely to stay, even though recent visibility is lacking.
The eighth-pallet display extends a familiar format the firm understands well, though it has not been visible since 2020, which suggests it may have been folded into custom work.

Wood lies outside the firm's paper-based knowledge base, which limits its ability to learn from results and improve the product, and with no visibility since 2020, resources are better returned to cardboard displays.
Despite familiar cardboard know-how, the media-product segment is shrinking, the product has not been visible since 2020, and the format is easily covered by the generic quarter-pallet displays.
